title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by attacker PowerShell on scranton and WMI/WinRM host on nashua
rationale: All four findings describe the same LSASS handle opens: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, pbeesly) on scranton with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff at 03:05:16Z and wsmprovhost.exe/python.exe on nashua with 0x1f3fff at 03:09:29Z. F16 and F31 are alternate interpretations of the same events; F55 adds the PsExec-pushed python.exe LSASS open and beacon. This is OS credential dumping from LSASS memory (T1003.001).

title: PowerShell keystroke logger and clipboard capture on scranton
rationale: pbeesly ran Get-Keystrokes (job 'Keystrokes') and Get-Clipboard on scranton — keylogging (T1056.001).

title: WebDAV forced authentication from scranton followed by SMB/ADMIN$ credential use against nashua and newyork
rationale: scranton (10.0.1.4) probed SMB then pivoted to WebDAV against 192.168.0.4 using DavClnt/MiniRedir user agents, followed by ADMIN$ access to nashua as pbeesly and SCRANTON$ activity on newyork — forced authentication to capture/relay credentials (T1187).

title: Steganographic hidden PowerShell stager (control.exe parent) that opened LSASS on scranton
rationale: Both findings describe the same process entity: the hidden, execution-policy-bypassing PowerShell (PID 2976) spawned by control.exe that decoded monkey.png and IEX'd the payload, then opened LSASS with full access. The credential-access action is exploitation/execution of the stager enabling credential access (T1212).

title: WMI remote-exec host opened LSASS on nashua
rationale: wsmprovhost.exe (pbeesly) created via WMI/WinRM remote execution opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF on nashua; the credential-access action is exploitation of the remote-execution channel to reach LSASS (T1212).

title: accesschk.exe credential reconnaissance creating passwordsDB and querying LSA registry key on scranton
rationale: Both findings describe the same accesschk.exe execution by pbeesly that created passwordsDB and queried HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Lsa — credential hunting for unsecured credentials on the host (T1552).

title: Plaintext password on PsExec64 command line used against NASHUA
rationale: Both findings describe the same PsExec64 invocations with -u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by in cleartext on the command line and in script blocks, producing 4648 logons on nashua — credentials in files/command lines (T1552.001).

title: Credential-named file collection and password-protected archive on nashua
rationale: PowerShell collected *pass*,*login*,*admin*,*vpn* files into working.zip and Rar.exe re-archived with a password, then sdelete64 wiped artifacts — searching for credentials in files (T1552.001).

title: PowerShell opened Microsoft Edge browser processes with full access on scranton
rationale: PowerShell (PID 2976) opened MicrosoftEdge.exe and its subprocesses with 0x1FFFFF during the intrusion, consistent with extracting credentials from the web browser (T1555.003).

title: Browser processes opened with full access on nashua
rationale: wsmprovhost (pbeesly) opened MicrosoftEdge.exe and MicrosoftEdgeCP.exe with 0x1f3fff on nashua, consistent with extracting credentials from the web browser (T1555.003).

title: Kerberos ticket requests for krbtgt alongside LSASS access on scranton
rationale: Full-access LSASS handles plus 4769 ticket requests for krbtgt from pbeesly on the DC indicate Kerberos ticket theft/forgery activity (T1558).

title: No SAML token forgery observed; certificate export is closest precursor
rationale: No SAML assertion or token artifacts were found; the only related activity is the private-key/certificate export, which is a precursor to forging SAML tokens (T1606.002).

title: Certificate/private-key export via Get-PrivateKeys on scranton
rationale: All three findings describe the same Get-PrivateKeys execution that enumerated cert:\LocalMachine and exported certificates with private keys to password-protected .pfx files (coyn5igj.3io.pfx), with F60 adding exfil staging — stealing authentication certificates (T1649).

title: In-memory DLL compilation via csc.exe on scranton
rationale: PowerShell invoked csc.exe to compile DLLs in the user Temp directory — this is obfuscated/compiled payload execution (T1027), not credential access.

title: Masqueraded .scr stager in ProgramData\victim on scranton
rationale: A masqueraded .scr launched from explorer spawned cmd/powershell to start the intrusion — this is execution/user execution (T1204), not credential access.

title: hostui.exe launched with -verb runas for elevation on scranton
rationale: PowerShell launched hostui.exe with -verb runas to force a UAC elevation prompt — privilege escalation (T1548), not credential access.

title: sdclt.exe spawned by cmd on scranton
rationale: sdclt.exe, a known UAC-bypass binary, was spawned by cmd during the intrusion — privilege escalation/UAC bypass (T1548), not credential access.
